nodes.label: Module 8 — Encounters & Visit Notes
nodes.rationale: The clinical record's documentation surface and the nervous-system trigger for clinical-record-driven downstream work; encounter.signed drives half the clinical phase (M9, M10, M14, M22, M28, M31, M33).

nodes.label: HearthNote Three-Layer Documentation Engine
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 deterministic is the structured source of truth, Layer 2 is an enhancement that diffs against Layer 1 and hard-blocks new facts, Layer 3 is the always-on signing-blocking compliance gate. Competitors' AI assistants produce plausible narrative with no seam to the underlying data, so surveyors cannot reconstruct what the clinician picked versus what the AI invented.

nodes.label: Layer-2 Eligibility Three-Flag AND + BAA Gate (D5, D6/M08-F01)
nodes.rationale: Tenant flag alone is too coarse for high-stakes notes and per-clinician only is too granular to audit; the three-flag AND lets a tenant adopt Layer 2 broadly while keeping F2F, admission and recert deterministic-only. No PHI may leave the perimeter until external.anthropic_baa_executed is set — the BAA is recorded as in negotiation, so layer2_eligibility_reason='baa_not_executed' and M32's cloud backend hard-refuses dispatch.

nodes.label: LLM Diff Hard-Block Category List (D7)
nodes.rationale: The three architecture categories (vitals, doses, codes) are insufficient — allergies and code status carry higher safety risk than vitals: a medication-dose error is at least detectable on read, whereas a silently swapped code-status statement may not be. Categories live in one typed constant so adding one is a deliberate reviewed change.

nodes.label: Addenda as First-Class Rows, Immutability After Sign (D2)
nodes.rationale: Surveyor reconstruction of 'what was signed at 4pm on the 12th' needs the row, not the row's edit history; allowing post-sign edits with an audit diff fails the strictest survey defense. An immutability trigger refuses UPDATEs to protected columns and all DELETEs.

nodes.label: Cosignature Workflow — 24h soft / 48h hard, billing-blocked (D3)
nodes.rationale: A 7-day window is too loose for survey defense and no hard cap creates aged billing that ages out; the supervisor-release path past 48 hours (with a ≥40-char documented reason) is the operational concession that makes the gate workable in real agencies.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Late-Entry Ladder (D4)
nodes.rationale: No limit invites fraudulent backdating; a hard 24-hour cap is clinically unrealistic for field staff with offline patches. Three tiers match the operational reality that most late entries are within 24 hours, a few are 1–14 days, and rare admin escalations exceed 14 days.

nodes.label: EVV-Authoritative Encounter Bracketing with Documented Fallback (D9)
nodes.rationale: When M18 events exist they are read-only truth and clinician-entered times cannot override; when absent, a ≥20-char evv_missing_reason is required. Clinician-entered-always defeats EVV; EVV-required breaks offline field work. Stricter than several competitors and earns straight survey defense in Cures Act §12006 states.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Version Pinned at First Finalize (D11)
nodes.rationale: Latest-version resolution would silently change historical notes when annual ICD-10 and biannual SNOMED updates ship, failing surveyor reconstruction. Pinning freezes the narrative like an immutable git ref — the analog of M7's hybrid versioning.

nodes.label: BillableEncounterReader Seam
nodes.rationale: M8 exposes a clean reader saying billable / not yet billable / not billable with a reason, factoring cosignature, late-entry, EVV and encounter type — without knowing HIPPS, revenue codes, 837I segments, SIA add-ons or cap math, all of which are M23/M24/M26.

nodes.label: SignedEncountersReader Seam (signedEncountersForPatientSince)
nodes.rationale: M8 is the source of truth, not the digest — the IDG aggregation content is owned by M14 and reads through this seam rather than M8 pre-aggregating.

nodes.label: F2F Dual-Write in One Transaction (D1)
nodes.rationale: Writing both the M8 clinical note and the M6 face_to_face_encounter in one transaction avoids losing HearthNote and EVV for the F2F note while avoiding bloating M8 with compliance fields; if either side's gate fails the transaction aborts and both panels surface remediation.

nodes.label: 5-Minute Step-Up Auth on Every Clinical Signature (D13)
nodes.rationale: No step-up fails 21 CFR Part 11 e-signature principles and CoP 418.104(c) authentication; 5 minutes matches M2's SESSION_POLICY screen-lock window so the whole session-class model stays symmetric.

nodes.label: Encounter Lifecycle State Machine & Layer-3 Signing Gate
nodes.rationale: draft → finalized → signed → cosign_pending → cosigned with addendum_open and voided branches. Before any encounter signs, the always-on Layer 3 gate checks required HearthNote sections per encounter type × discipline, required vitals, required HOPE items, required scales, the LPN/CHHA cosignature row, the late-entry reason, and fresh step-up authentication; failures return 422 with structured remediation hints.
